bounds.domain: One Android deployment, one saved key and one renewal at a time. At most two renewal requests on two days, three acknowledgement rounds per renewal, one sign-in attempt that starts meanwhile, one newer credential action (a sign-out or a sign-in that replaces the saved key), one deadline and one plugin close. Renewal answers are a code, a refusal of the renewal (403, 409), a refusal of the key itself (401) or no usable answer. Cloud's rules for the keys of one sign-in are part of the model: it ends the sign-in when a key without a confirmed successor revokes itself or when a key asks for renewal after its successor was confirmed, and it ends the old key alone when the old key's revocation names the new one. Acknowledgement answers are confirmed, already complete, retryable, refused, or confirmed at Cloud with the answer lost.
bounds.assumptions: The host's credential intent fence orders a renewal's guarded save against any newer credential action: the save and the action never interleave. The store compares the saved key with the one the renewal presented in the same guarded step. A day is projected to the nextDay event and Cloud's acknowledgement deadline to the deadline event. The inline and background acknowledgement rounds are one bounded sequence.
bounds.limitations: Revocation requests take effect at Cloud when they are sent; a lost revocation is not modeled. The model ends at the first revocation of the replaced key: the stored duty to revoke it (written before the save with the new key's id, retried in this process and on later starts with that id, ended by a 2xx or a 401 answer, never applied to a key that is still the saved one or to a duty that names no successor), Cloud's two-minute tolerance for an unnamed last step and the host's savedKeyRenewed hook run in the JVM fixtures only, the first against a model of Cloud's rules. A confirmed key that was never saved stays active at Cloud, unused, until the sign-in ends or it expires; the saved key is then not renewed again and the owner signs in when it expires. The owner's own sign-out or sign-in is modeled as a change of the saved key only, not as its revocation requests. The expiry warning, the preference record, the hourly automatic check, a pending browser sign-in from an earlier process, other deployments and overlapping plugin instances are outside this model. The JVM fixtures run the exact renewal methods against synthetic slot, HTTPS and lifecycle ports, and the exact save through plugin-native-agent's ResidentCredentialStore; they do not run Android or contact Cloud.
